releaseNotes: spine.md exists, and SKILL.md is 2,683 bytes smaller. ARCHITECTURE.md target layout has named spine.md — the ordered walk through a launch — since the north star was written, and it did not exist; the stage sequence was a 20-row table inside SKILL.md, which loads on every trigger whether or not the question is what comes next. The table moves to spine.md with the routing contract restated at its head: it answers what comes next, SKILL.md answers what governs this, and it is not to be preloaded and worked through top to bottom.

The Runtime Routing And Dynamic Workflows section was a 2,006-byte summary of playbook/process/dynamic-workflows.md, a 20KB reference it already linked to. SKILL.md keeps the always-on kernel — Claude for pre-build, Codex for the core build, a bias and not a gate, record the split in ORCHESTRATION.md, never downgrade quality because a runtime lacks workflows — and routes the rest. Verified no content was lost: the reference already carries the non-Claude-Code surfacing protocol, the trigger list, token budgets, quarantine, the 2.1.154 fallback, stop-at-the-spec, and producer-verifier separation.

Start Here was deliberately NOT collapsed, and this is worth recording because it looks like the obvious next 1,700 bytes. Items 4 to 6 read like routing duplicates of the operations and trust rows in Lane Routing, but they are not: Lane Routing indexes the reference, while Start Here carries the TRIGGER — before any API key, token, OAuth credential, webhook signing secret, or local .env. Collapsing them would leave an agent able to touch a credential without loading secrets management. That is a real regression to buy back a small number of bytes.

The 12KB entrypoint target in ARCHITECTURE.md is not reachable without losing something real, and the arithmetic is now measured rather than assumed. SKILL.md is 19,963 bytes after this change. Lane Routing is already collapsed to 15 index-pointing rows at roughly 246 bytes each from the v0.53.0 pass, so there is little left there. What remains is Ground Rules (3,073), the five always-on contracts (4,130), Lane Routing (3,696) and What Counts As Done (1,306) — reaching 12,288 means roughly halving two of them. The target was written when SKILL.md was 46,975 bytes, before the playbook collapse; it is an aspiration set pre-contact, not a measured floor. Recommend amending it with evidence rather than cutting into routing rows or always-on contracts; deliberately not amended here, because changing a stated target is the founder call.

Review round caught a real regression in the extraction, and it is the exact failure mode that makes entrypoint cuts dangerous. The first pass routed the non-Claude-Code protocol — surface the Claude recommendation once, record it in PROJECT_STATE.yaml, continue regardless — behind a load trigger reading "before proposing or running a workflow". But Codex cannot run workflows at all, so for the one runtime that protocol exists to serve, the trigger never fires: an agent doing ordinary pre-build work on Codex would never surface or record anything. The protocol is back in the always-on kernel and the load trigger now also fires when starting any pre-build stage on a non-Claude runtime. Net saving drops from 3,222 to 2,683 bytes; correctness is worth the 539.

The prose fix was not enough, and the review was right to escalate it. Repairing the runtime-routing regression in SKILL.md left nothing stopping the next compaction from re-making the identical cut, because no gate asserted the trigger existed — audit:ci had already stayed green straight through the first one. The trigger is now pinned as four required_terms in machine/evals/triggering/autopilot-triggering.yaml, which check-autopilot-contract already asserts against SKILL.md body text, plus a failing fixture that strips the phrase and proves the gate fails with autopilot.body.required_term_missing. Fixture count 723 to 724.

One wrinkle worth recording for whoever compresses SKILL.md next: required_terms are matched against raw file text, and SKILL.md is hard-wrapped, so a term spanning a line break fails on reflow alone rather than on meaning. The first attempt at pinning this used continue in the current runtime regardless, which wraps; it was narrowed to current runtime regardless, and the constraint is now noted in the yaml itself.

The entrypoint ceiling is ratcheted 45KB to 20KB, which is the half of this change that actually holds it. Extracting 2,683 bytes while check-reference-size still permitted 45KB meant roughly 25KB could flow straight back into the file that loads on every trigger with the gate staying green — the freeze-and-subtract policy the validator comment describes, defeated by not applying it. ARCHITECTURE.md now states the rule as a ratchet rather than a target: the ceiling sits just above current size and every extraction lowers it in the same commit.

The 12KB entrypoint target is retired with its measurement recorded. It was written when SKILL.md was 46,975 bytes, before the playbook collapse. At 20,057 bytes the remainder is Lane Routing 3,696 (already collapsed to 15 index rows at roughly 246 bytes each, no slack), five always-on contracts 4,130, Ground Rules 3,073, What Counts As Done 1,306 — reaching 12,288 means halving two of those. The obvious-looking candidate is a trap and is now documented as one: Start Here items 4 to 6 read like duplicates of the operations and trust routing rows, but Lane Routing indexes the reference while Start Here carries the trigger, so collapsing them lets an agent touch a credential without loading secrets management.

The workflow load trigger was wrong on BOTH sides, not just the non-Claude one. Hanging it on "before proposing or running a workflow" meant that on Claude Code it fired after the selection decision the reference exists to inform, and on Codex it never fired at all. It now fires when starting any pre-build stage, with both halves pinned as required terms, and the once-only PROJECT_STATE record is pinned too — without that term a compaction could drop the recording instruction while every other term still passed, letting a later session repeat the recommendation. Each new term was individually proven to fail the gate when removed.
